title: Fluency: the difference of two squares

families.skill: factorise a difference of two squares

wrong.line: That square has two middle strips of $-{p*q:c}{v}$; in a difference of squares the strips cancel.
That is $({p:c}{v}+{q})^2$, which has a middle term: one bracket needs a plus and one a minus.

solution: ${p2:c}{v}^2$ is the square of ${p:c}{v}$, and ${q2}$ is the square of ${q}$.
A square minus a square is a sum times a difference: ${poly(v; p2, 0, -q2)} = ({p:c}{v}+{q})({p:c}{v}-{q})$.

families.skill: factorise a number minus a square

wrong.line: That expands to ${poly(v; p2, 0, -q2)}$, the negative of the question: keep ${q}$ first in each bracket.
That square has two middle strips; in a difference of squares the strips cancel.

solution: ${q2}$ is the square of ${q}$, and ${p2:c}{v}^2$ is the square of ${p:c}{v}$.

families.skill: work out a difference of squares in your head

wrong.line: That is $({a} - {b})^2$: the difference of the squares is a sum times a difference.
That is ${a} + {b}$ alone: multiply it by ${a} - {b} = {d}$.

families.skill: take out a common factor, then use the difference of squares

wrong.line: Those brackets multiply to the expression divided by ${k}$: keep ${k}$ in front.
That square has two middle strips; in a difference of squares the strips cancel.

solution: Both terms divide by ${k}$: ${poly(v; a, 0, -c)} = {k}({poly(v; p2, 0, -q2)})$.
That bracket is a difference of two squares: ${poly(v; p2, 0, -q2)} = ({p:c}{v}+{q})({p:c}{v}-{q})$.
